verdicts.where: Three kinds of harm each with its own counter is stock (bludgeoning, piercing, slashing in D&D); 'only the pillar saves you from the dragon's breath' is the stock line-of-sight beat of film and raid; chosen stances in Nioh. Protection that simply follows what the feet are doing, for enemies too, I cannot place.

World of Darkness tabletop horror (Vampire: The Masquerade, Chronicles of Darkness): bashing, lethal and aggravated damage - three depths that heal at three speeds, are soaked less the deeper they go, and overflowing bashing is upgraded to lethal. Also the recharging shield over health of Halo.
verdicts.mutation: Drop the three-rung ladder and its overflow rule: let every wound keep the exact warning time it was shown for, and mend only when the player has stood still that many seconds on the spot where it landed, so harm is a debt in seconds owed to a place and not a tier.

verdicts.where: The Pied Piper's train; leading the herd down the road in The Walking Dead; MMO players 'training' monsters (EverQuest's 'train to zone'). A condition earned only by being followed along the wake, which makes the follower riper and faster, is in none of them.

Keeping measure (ma-ai) in fencing and samurai duels, where two fighters hold one distance and read each other; sweet-spot ranges such as the tip of Marth's sword. Spacing held over time that buys earlier warnings is its own.

Folk circumambulation: thrice sunwise (deasil) to bless or bind, widdershins to undo or curse - Burd Ellen taken for running widdershins round the church in Childe Rowland, 'weave a circle round him thrice' in Kubla Khan; Joshua circling Jericho before the blow. The fiction is the old rite itself; the build-and-spend rule laid on it is new.

The Old Man of the Sea riding Sinbad's shoulders; the stock chase beat of scraping a clinging attacker off against a wall or a low branch; Zelda's Morths (The Wind Waker) and Poison Mites (Twilight Princess), which cling and slow until shaken off. A cure that is a place and a pace is its own.

Snowspeeders winding tow-cable round the AT-AT's legs in The Empire Strikes Back; the cartoon chase in which pursuers following a looping runner end up tied in a knot; Pokemon Ranger's drawn loops; soul-link curses that share harm. Crossing your own wake as the act that ties is its own.

The sound- or motion-hunting monster that loses a victim who freezes and then goes to the latest noise: Tremors' graboids, A Quiet Place, the T. rex of Jurassic Park ('don't move'), The Descent's crawlers, the clickers of The Last of Us. As a no-button rule it is also Teemo's stand-still camouflage in League of Legends.

Body-named stat sets in tabletop games (head, heart and hands triads); one percent per point and a stat needed to use gear are the stock Diablo attribute. Attributes that measure kinds of moment (still, moving, near, timed) I cannot place in any story or game.

Tron's light cycles (the 1982 film and every game since): long straights and sharp corners that leave walls punishing whatever crosses them. Also the rope stretched across the road to unhorse riders (Sleepy Hollow, the Ewoks' trip-lines). Length-as-strength and the turn that pegs are the fresh part.
verdicts.mutation: Make it a rope and not a wall: a pegged line lies slack and harmless, and only the next straight walked directly away from its peg hauls it taut for as long as that walk lasts, so harm comes from pulling a line laid earlier instead of from leaving a trail.

verdicts.where: The thief's backstab from hiding (the D&D rogue, Ambush in World of Warcraft) joined to stand-still invisibility that pays a bonus when broken - Teemo's passive in League of Legends, the Spy's Cloak and Dagger in Team Fortress 2. The funeral mute as a figure is in Oliver Twist (Oliver walks as Sowerberry's mute), though not as a fighter.
verdicts.mutation: Drop the back-stab test: Last Word strikes everything that crossed an unseen threshold line through the Mute's shoulders while it stood, growing per crosser and not per second, so the class counts who came through the door it kept instead of whose back is turned.

verdicts.where: The lamplighter of The Little Prince, bound to relight a lamp that a relentless clock keeps putting out; the leeries of Mary Poppins Returns; Stevenson's 'The Lamplighter'. Timed light-all-the-torches puzzles in Zelda and capture-point upkeep in shooters. A class that is a route and a timetable round fixed posts is its own.

The stock shield-bearer: big shield in front, bare back, shield bash - hoplites and riot shields in fiction, Reinhardt in Overwatch, Mars's Bulwark in Dota 2 (harm cut by facing), lance and greatshield play in Monster Hunter and Dark Souls. Only the coffin plank is new.
verdicts.mutation: Fix the guarded arc to the compass bearing walked at the last toll instead of to the facing: for that whole toll period the bier guards one side of the world, drawn on the ground, and the player must keep the crowd on that side until the bell lets them choose again.

verdicts.where: Meteor-hammer and chain-weapon duels in which the swung weight kills at its arc and is useless inside it (Gogo Yubari in Kill Bill); the 'get inside the reach' rule of every spear and whip fight; Mark Twain's leadsman for the figure; orbiting weapons in Vampire Survivors. An orbit with a bare middle as a whole class is its own.

The feigned retreat that wheels on strung-out pursuers: Livy's last Horatius turning on the three Curiatii, the Parthian shot, the Normans at Hastings; the Pied Piper's train. Maugham's 'The Verger' has the figure only. A reversal as the trigger with the train's length as the multiplier is its own.

Mudlarks in Mayhew and Dickens (the river scavengers of Our Mutual Friend), Pratchett's Dodger; the hoard that makes its keeper stronger (Smaug's jewelled belly); greed-scaling items such as Money = Power in The Binding of Isaac. Attacking only by picking things up is its own.

Joshua's circuits of Jericho before the walls fall; the cartoon wind-up punch; Hugo Cabret winding the station clocks for the figure; full-circle stick motions in fighting games and drawn circles in Pokemon Ranger. Walked loops whose direction means wind or release are its own.

The closed warding figure that holds spirits inside it: the Triangle of Art of the Goetia, the devil's trap of Supernatural, the chalk or salt circle of every exorcism story. In games, capture by enclosure in Qix and Pokemon Ranger.
verdicts.mutation: Make the closed triangle a drawstring and not a ward: its three lines slide inward for 4 s, dragging what is inside toward the centre, and one hit lands when they meet, scaled by how much ground was drawn shut.

verdicts.where: Standing still while the procession of the dead goes by (the Wild Hunt, Galicia's Santa Compana); silent takedowns that do not alert the pack in stealth fiction (Assassin's Creed, Dishonored); graze scoring in Touhou. Being paid for being brushed past while motionless is its own.

Grimm's 'Godfather Death', where a life is a candle and death is its snuffing; the stock 'kill the lights and slip away' escape; detonating your own totems or traps in action role-playing games. Cashing in a standing bonus by its age at a fixed post is its own.

The Spartans' wall of Persian dead in 300 and the corpse barricades of zombie films; the necromancer's Bone Wall in Diablo II and Magic's Wall of Corpses; pick-up-again deployable shields in Rainbow Six Siege; the bier rested at the lychgate. A wall carried along, paid for in kills and set down by stopping is its own.

Distant only: a sniper zeroing the scope to a ranged target, naval ranging shots before firing for effect, the leadsman calling the mark in Mark Twain. I know nothing in which an approaching enemy sets the weapon's reach.

Follow-the-leader and Grandmother's Footsteps; a drill column halting on its leader; the Pied Piper's children; SUPERHOT, where the world moves only when you move. Halting only those the player has been leading, flanks left alive, is its own.

Final Fantasy's Throw command (the Ninja hurls weapons out of the pack, consumed, harm by the item's worth) and Gil Toss; Pokemon's Fling; Terraria's Coin Gun. In story, Hippomenes throwing away the golden apples to win the race with Atalanta.
verdicts.mutation: Do not burn the find for one burst: cast it down as a standing charge that bursts and loses one notch each time the player's path re-crosses it, and that can be picked up again with whatever notches are left, so the item is whittled and not spent.

verdicts.where: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, where the player slows or hurries the bell-tower town's public doom clock (Inverted Song of Time, Song of Double Time); Superman circling the Earth backwards to wind time back; Hermione's Time-Turner counted in turns; time-extension pickups in arcade racers.
verdicts.mutation: Do not move the clock's hands, move its aim: circles walked round the bell-post step the next surge's entry door one radial stone sunwise or widdershins, and circles round a gate move that gate, so the Regulator edits where the bell strikes and never when.

verdicts.where: Wile E. Coyote's X-marked spot under the falling anvil, to which the quarry must be led back; ramping turrets and traps left in place in action role-playing games; the plumb line of Amos for the image. A mark set only by the last deliberate stop is its own.

The tow-cable round the AT-AT's legs in The Empire Strikes Back; the lasso, and the Looney Tunes chase tied in a knot; closing loops in Pokemon Ranger and Qix. A strike on the crossing point itself, with no loop needed, is its own.

The Parthian shot loosed backwards from a straight gallop; 'Stay on target' in the Death Star trench, the reward for refusing to swerve; fore-and-aft weapons in Vampire Survivors. The rear shot as a meter of unturned seconds is its own.

Scylla and Charybdis and the Clashing Rocks, the passage between two dangers; the stock fight gag of slipping between two attackers so that they strike each other; graze bonuses in Touhou. A near miss that must be between a pair, who then give the shot its line, is its own.

The iaido showdown of samurai film: long stillness, then one step and one cut (Sanjuro's last duel, Zatoichi); the dragon's drawn breath before the flame; hold-and-release charge shots (Mega Man). Stillness as the charge and the first step as the aim is its own.

The Westminster Quarters, whose chime grows longer each quarter until the hour; clock jacks striking the quarters (Jack Blandiver at Wells); Poe's ebony clock in 'The Masque of the Red Death'; periodic pulse weapons in survivor games. A pulse that keeps the run's public time is its own.

Distant only: the scales of judgement (Anubis weighing the heart, 'weighed in the balances and found wanting'); balance meters such as the Eclipse druid in World of Warcraft. I know nothing that spends the size of one crowd on the other.

Knocking spirits in the rock (Cornish knockers, King's The Tommyknockers); the knocker-up with her pole (the picture book Mary Smith); earthbenders striking stone so the blow comes out of the far side (Avatar: The Last Airbender); totem-origin spells and bank shots. The obstacle as origin with a weak near side is its own.

The steel cable strung between two cars to scythe a herd of walkers in The Walking Dead; a chain between two riders; the maypole and tetherball sweep; tether beams between co-op partners. One end pinned where you stood and the other swung by walking is its own.

'The Appointment in Samarra' (Maugham's retelling): a meeting kept at a fixed place and hour; raid 'soak' circles that must be stood in as they close (World of Warcraft, Final Fantasy XIV); stand-in-the-circle shrines. A strike that is weak unless the player keeps the appointment is its own.

Tolstoy's 'How Much Land Does a Man Need?', where the land is whatever you can walk round and greed for wide bounds is the danger; Dido's oxhide; the Rogationtide beating of the bounds; territory by path in Qix. Taking only the four extremes of a walk as the strike box is its own.

The Road Runner's dead stop that sends the chaser sailing past; momentum-then-release effects (the Momentum support in Path of Exile) and ground-pounds on landing. The lifted thumb as the only trigger is its own.
'Hold... hold... now!' - the held volley of every film battle (Braveheart); trigger and charge-storing supports in Path of Exile. The player's own stop as the trigger is its own.

Ekko's trailing afterimage of where he stood seconds ago (League of Legends, Arcane); Peter Pan's shadow acting apart from him; Dragon Ball's afterimages; Mirage Archer in Path of Exile; the Cosmic Clones of Super Mario Galaxy 2. A past self as caster, blind around the present self, is its own.

'Stay on target' and the steady bombing run (Star Wars, The Dam Busters); a broadside that needs a held course; while-moving bonuses in survivor games. Paying for not turning and charging a silence for each corner is its own.

The nymph Echo answering from the rocks; 'the stone shall cry out of the wall' (Habakkuk 2:11); Spell Echo and Spell Totem in Path of Exile. A repeat thrown back from whatever stone stands nearest is its own.

Money as ammunition: Final Fantasy's Gil Toss, Terraria's Coin Gun, the Microtransaction Gun in Enter the Gungeon, coin-fed items in The Binding of Isaac. In story it is the mercenary's and the ferryman's bargain, a coin for every stroke.
verdicts.mutation: Do not burn the coin: each cast flings one carried coin out with the hit, so it lies where the sigil struck among the dead and sinks at the next toll unless walked back for; harm is bought with reach and a return trip, not with a purchase.

verdicts.where: Graze systems that load the weapon on near misses: Psyvariar's Buzz, the tension shot of Shikigami no Shiro, graze in Touhou; perfect-dodge rewards such as Witch Time in Bayonetta. In story it is the bullet that parts the hero's hair.
verdicts.mutation: Count the miss by whom it hit instead: the sigil gains a cast for each other enemy caught inside a shown strike that missed the player, so the player stands where a keeper's blow will fall on its own dead.

verdicts.where: Clock figures that stand idle and all strike together on the quarter; Poe's revellers stopped by each chime; stored-damage detonation skills. A release the player cannot hurry because the district's clock holds the trigger is its own.

The Benedictine vow of stability and the anchorite's cell; power kept by a promise and lost by breaking it - the Irish geas, the paladin's oath, Nen 'vows and limitations' in Hunter x Hunter, binding vows in Jujutsu Kaisen, the Vows of Hades II; mana reservation in Path of Exile. Warning time as the pool that is reserved is its own.

The Vow of Poverty of Dungeons & Dragons 3.5 (Book of Exalted Deeds) and the monk vows of Pathfinder: own next to nothing, gain standing bonuses, lose them the moment the vow is broken - the same name and the same bargain; the mendicant friar behind them; NetHack's conducts.
verdicts.mutation: Make it a vow of alms and not of lack: the promise is to leave the first find of each toll period lying where it fell; each find left stands as a small cairn that pays the bonus while unclaimed, and walking back to take one breaks the vow.

verdicts.where: The hatch button of LOST, pressed every 108 minutes or else; the night-watchman's tell-tale clock rounds; the Angelus rung without fail; streak bonuses that reset on a miss. A streak whose beat is a journey to the district's bell-post is its own.

'Cast thy bread upon the waters, for thou shalt find it after many days' and the tithe returned a hundredfold; the parable of the talents; Dark Souls bloodstains and Shovel Knight's dropped gold bags. A small bell-timed drop that pays double for a well-timed return is its own.

Wave-entrance markers in tower defence (the skull flags of Kingdom Rush); stand-in-the-circle shrines and the teleporter zone of Risk of Rain; the omen that shows where the blow will fall. One ring that is both forecast and dare is its own.
Active reload in Gears of War; the rocket start timed on the lights in Mario Kart; a counted rest in music. A timing window measured in stillness is its own.

Refusing the banker in Deal or No Deal; 'one more room' push-your-luck delving; choosing to loop rather than leave in Risk of Rain; in story, the offer three times refused. A refusal recorded as a notch on every later gate is its own.

Hallowed ground the dead cannot profane (vampire lore, the holy-ground rule of Highlander); 'home base' in tag; Consecration in Diablo and bonfires in Dark Souls. Shelters left behind wherever a level was taken is its own.

Tilt to walk, push to run on the analog stick of Super Mario 64; sprinting lowers the weapon in Call of Duty; fight or flight. Both are everyday parts; putting them on the one steering thumb of an auto-attack game is a small step of its own.

The marching-band countermarch, files reversing back through their own ranks; the matador's pass that turns the bull; Red Rover; dodge-roll invulnerability frames. A U-turn as the dodge that also turns the crowd is its own.

Romero's shuffling dead and the herds of The Walking Dead arriving where you were; lag pursuit; Celeste's Badeline chasers and the Cosmic Clones of Super Mario Galaxy 2, which trail your past self; Pac-Man's offset targeting. A whole horde aimed 1.2 s behind the body is its own.

Red Light, Green Light with a gun: the doll of Squid Game, here hearing instead of seeing. The eyeless listener is the creature of A Quiet Place (head plates lifting to hear), the crawlers of The Descent, the Pale Man of Pan's Labyrinth.

The tracking hound thrown off by a quarry that doubles back across its own trail: fox-hunting lore, Rainsford's looped trail in 'The Most Dangerous Game', the bloodhounds of Cool Hand Luke. In games, pursuers that replay your path (Cosmic Clones, Celeste's Badeline).
verdicts.mutation: Make it a trail-eater and not a trail-follower: it consumes the player's wake as it runs it, so nothing behind it counts for In Procession, Knotted or Hitch, and where the path crosses itself it swallows the knot and chokes for 3 s.

verdicts.where: Zoolander, who 'can't turn left'; the fiddler crab's one great claw; the one-armed Fachan of Highland lore; the slow-turning brute you circle-strafe (Zelda's Iron Knuckle, every Dark Souls backstab). An enemy built left or right that makes the direction of the circle the whole question is its own.

Red Rover's hand-linked line; the Danse Macabre chain of the dead (the last shot of The Seventh Seal); Marley's ghost and the chain gang; link-boys for the name; laser fences between pylons, beam-linked elites in Diablo III, bullet-hell walls with gaps. One advancing row of chains and holes is its own.

The 'donut' attack of raid and hunting games, a deadly ring that is safe at the feet: the dynamo attacks of Final Fantasy XIV, tail spins in Monster Hunter, Zelda's Ball and Chain Trooper. In story, stepping inside the swing of the giant's club or Little John's staff.
verdicts.mutation: Hold the pole a third of the way along, so the sweep has a long arm and a short arm on opposite sides: the safe ground is not a disc at its feet but a crescent that turns with the pole, and the player must walk round with the short end.

verdicts.where: The guard who must be stopped before he reaches the alarm bell: the bell-ringers of Assassin's Creed, the sentry running for the gong or horn in every infiltration film; runners that leak past in tower defence.
verdicts.mutation: Let it steal the hour instead of ringing it: it drags the bell's clapper from the post toward the district's edge, each 10 m shortening every later toll interval by 2 s, until the player kills it and walks the clapper back to the post.

verdicts.where: The pod person who points and shrieks to bring the others in Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1978); the screamer zombie that calls the horde (State of Decay, 7 Days to Die); the artillery spotter and the pointer dog.
verdicts.mutation: Have its arm point not at the player but 1.2 s ahead along the player's heading, with the dead steering at that point: the player beats it by feinting so the arm points wrong, not by walking out to kill it.

verdicts.where: Clock jacks (Jack Blandiver at Wells, Jack the Smiter at Southwold); the marching hammers of Pink Floyd's The Wall; Wagner's Nibelheim anvils; beat blocks in Super Mario 3D World and the shared beat of Crypt of the NecroDancer. One pulse shared by every Jack in the district is its own.

The threshold guardian and toll-taker: the bridge troll of the Billy Goats Gruff, Charon wanting his obol, the customs man; the hoard-dragon roused by one stolen cup (Beowulf, Smaug); Spelunky's shopkeepers waiting at the exit. A guard that exists only because of the load, and is as strong as the load, is its own.

The nation-wide circle closed around its victims in Fullmetal Alchemist; the encircling coil of slither.io and the serpent boss hurt only at one end (Zelda's Moldorm); Qix inside out; beating the bounds. A keeper that perambulates the player, with corner stakes to break, is its own.

Change ringing as told in Sayers' The Nine Tailors, neighbouring bells swapping each row; Simon-style pattern bosses; enemy intents in Slay the Spire; numbered-order raid mechanics in Final Fantasy XIV. A published real-time queue that changes by one visible swap is its own.

Charon, ferryman of the dead with pole and lantern (Dante's beats with his oar any soul that lags; the lantern-bearing Ferryman of Sea of Thieves), joined to the stock 'stay in the light or the dark takes you' of Pitch Black, Doctor Who's Vashta Nerada, A Plague Tale and Ori. The safe band with a deadly middle is the fresh part.
verdicts.mutation: Lose the ferryman: make the keeper a diving bell lowered on a chain into the flooded street, with air only in a ring under its rim; the band is the air, the deadly middle is the clapper's swing, and in phase 3 the bell is hauled across the district with the player walking under it.

verdicts.where: Dark City, whose streets are rearranged at each midnight, and the nightly shifting walls of The Maze Runner; the Hot Gates and the Oldboy corridor, where foes can only come from the ends; real ropewalks (Chatham's ropery, Longfellow's 'The Ropewalk'). A district of two-ended lanes rejoined by the bell is its own.

The sundial plaza; 'stay out of the shadows' (Doctor Who's Vashta Nerada, Pitch Black); clock-face arenas with a sweeping hand (Castlevania's clock tower); the prison-yard searchlight turned inside out. Night as a wedge a few metres away whose edge is the clock's hand is its own.

The flooded pillared cistern or crypt of gothic fiction and games (Istanbul's Basilica Cistern in From Russia with Love and Dan Brown's Inferno, Moria's pillared halls) plus the noise lure of every stealth story: slinging stones at metal to draw guards in A Plague Tale, Pippin's stone down the well.
verdicts.mutation: Let the ring travel: a struck pillar rings, then passes its ring to the next pillar along the grid line away from the face that was struck, four pillars in turn, drawing the dead down that aisle, so the player sends a crowd along a chosen colonnade by choosing which face to strike.

verdicts.where: Ariadne's single thread, paid out and followed back; the one-path labyrinth set in the floor at Chartres; the Sphere Grid walk of Final Fantasy X; the one-line puzzles of The Witness. A whole build as one unbranching walk, taken back only from its head, is its own.

Dido's oxhide, the most ground the least fence can hold; territory by enclosure in Go and Qix; the Thread of Hope ring in Path of Exile; beating the parish bounds. Fencing a cluster of nodes with the route itself is its own.

A tree's yearly rings and Dante's circles for the picture; time-gated power such as the Gathering Storm rune in League of Legends; late-scaling items. Rings that switch on at a stated toll of the run's public clock are its own.

Ley lines (Watkins' The Old Straight Track), power running along straight alignments; five-in-a-row; row and column bonuses in Backpack Hero and adjacency in city builders. Counting one unbroken straight street through a node is its own.

The gunfighter's notched grip and the Exchequer tally stick; legacy items that grow with their bearer (Earthdawn thread items, Weapons of Legacy in D&D); Hades keepsakes ranking up with encounters carried; the found-in-raid rule of Escape from Tarkov. Worth counted purely in tolls dared is its own.

Raising a Digimon or a Chao, where what you did most decides what it becomes; Dwarf Fortress artifacts engraved with their own history; Riven challenges in Warframe; the wand that 'learns from its wielder' in Harry Potter; use-based skills in The Elder Scrolls. A line that works only in the posture that wrote it is its own.

Shiren the Wanderer and the Mystery Dungeon line: stored gear is bettered only by carrying it back into a run, and is lost whole on death; gamble-upgrades that can destroy the item (the Vaal Orb in Path of Exile, enhancement in Korean online games). In story, the blade that must go back to the fire that made it.
verdicts.mutation: Stake lines and not the item: dying in the re-walk erases the struck line and its two neighbours for good and leaves the rest, so the order in which an item was written decides what each rewrite puts at risk.

verdicts.where: The two-minute Armistice silence and the Christmas truce of 1914; Poe's 'Masque of the Red Death', where all stand still while the clock chimes; the fairy-tale test of leaving the helpless feast untouched (Pan's Labyrinth); harvest-or-rescue in BioShock; the Orologion freeze of Vampire Survivors. A free freeze that pays only if honoured is its own.

The phantom funeral that sweeps the walker along: the Welsh toili, Galicia's Santa Compana, Hawaii's Night Marchers, Japan's Hyakki Yagyo; the rule never to cut through a cortege; blending into a walking group of scholars in Assassin's Creed. Matching a half pace with the thumb for a reward is its own.

'Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way' (Matthew 7:14) and Bunyan's Wicket Gate; timed doors in Dead Cells, Erebus gates in Hades, high-risk exits in extraction shooters. Two doors open on one short clock, the better one beyond the crowd, is its own in arrangement only.

The Red Sea closing on Pharaoh's host once the pursued are through; the portcullis dropped on the pursuers; Rome's beaten armies 'passing under the yoke'; the lychgate custom; kill-gates in trap games (Orcs Must Die). A trap that fires once, only behind the player, and pays by the train's length is its own.

Church sanctuary as every reader knows it: Quasimodo's 'Sanctuary!' at Notre-Dame and the Durham knocker itself; 'home base' in tag; safe rooms where nothing can follow (Resident Evil, Left 4 Dead); the invulnerable but pacified bubble of World of Warcraft.
verdicts.mutation: Give the real sequel to sanctuary, abjuration: the knock assigns a far gate and draws a straight road to it; nothing may touch the player while on that road, stepping off ends the protection, and the road leads out of the vigil, so sanctuary is a guarded way out and not a pause.

verdicts.where: Defoe's A Journal of the Plague Year, which quotes the Bills; Edge of Tomorrow and Re:Zero, where each death teaches the blow that dealt it; the Morgue of Don't Starve and the graveyard of Darkest Dungeon; Dark Souls bloodstains. A death that permanently lengthens the warning of its own cause is its own.

Hearn's 'The Soul of the Great Bell', the girl cast into the bronze who becomes its voice; Donne's passing bell and Sayers' Nine Tailors tolling a life; ancestors as traits in Rogue Legacy, fallen heroes' relics in Massive Chalice, legacy boons in State of Decay 2. A carillon in which each bell is one dead character and how it was played is its own.

Per-wave rewards that are permanent the moment the wave is passed and survive defeat or quitting: round experience in Bloons TD 6 and Call of Duty Zombies, time-survived payouts in mobile survivor games, gold kept on death in Vampire Survivors. In story, the watchman paid by the hour struck.
verdicts.mutation: Pay each toll's Echoes into the bell that rang, not to the account: they hang in that district's bell, safe at once, and are collected by the next character who hears the same numbered toll there, so the currency is always inherited by a later life.

verdicts.where: The three caskets of The Merchant of Venice and 'choose wisely' in the Grail chamber; choose-one pedestals in The Binding of Isaac; unpaused item picks in Risk of Rain 2 (Artifact of Command); reward doors in Hades. Every level-up as a timed walk inside the horde is its own.

The teleporter charge of Risk of Rain and the exit countdown of Escape from Tarkov; the looter too laden to get out before the door shuts (Beni in The Mummy, the Cave of Wonders, Chaucer's Pardoner's Tale); encumbrance rules. An exit timer sized by the load is its own.

Millet's 'The Angelus', where work stops and all stand still at the bell; the minute's silence; musical statues; Poe's revellers frozen by the chime; on-the-beat bonuses in rhythm-action games. One exact act of stillness on a 75 s stroke is its own.

Marlowe's Faustus counting the hour until the clock strikes; Cinderella's midnight; Albrecht saved by the dawn bell in Giselle; the Doom countdown of Final Fantasy; Fight For Your Life in Borderlands; the End Game Collapse of Dead by Daylight. A reprieve as long as whatever the bell has left, paid for with the haul, is its own.

A sop thrown to Cerberus, Atalanta's golden apples, the sledge passengers thrown to the wolves in My Antonia; the Monkey Bomb of Call of Duty Zombies and the pipe bomb of Left 4 Dead; the stealth-game crouch-walk and the held volley. Each half is familiar; buttons that only take away is the part that is its own.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, where the tutorial watches how you fought and proposes a class; Dungeon Siege naming your class from what you used; the Sorting Hat, and the Ceremony of Twelve in The Giver, where the elders assign a calling from observed habits; the virtue questions of Ultima IV.
verdicts.mutation: Let the refusal matter: the two measured classes rise as two of the district's dead tradespeople where the player did those acts most; the class is taken by standing in one's place for 2 s, and the one refused walks the district as a rival using its starting sigil against the player.
